problems.title: RSK mean baseline0.21 incompatible with full-permutation binary-inversion MSE protocol
problems.evidence: For every inversion bit ap+(1-a)q=1/2; test MSE=1/4+(1+a)/(1-a)(p-1/2)^2>=1/4.
problems.counterevidence: Unstated encoding/filtering/scaling or table typo could explain discrepancy; no fabrication claim.
problems.dependency: RSK target identity and model difficulty/baseline comparison.
problems.repair: Release exact representation, partition and MSE reduction; recompute or correct table. Historical implementation unavailable.

independent_verification.source_claim: Reread p14 Table3 .21 mean baseline, p19 binary-inversion regression, p34 all-permutation coverage; actual loader inversion_vector and RSK notebook cells1,4-6 corroborate pairing and exhaustive disjoint split.
independent_verification.assumptions_verified: Unweighted exhaustive permutations, disjoint nonempty training/test partition, coordinate training means, coordinate-averaged squared loss. Current loader pads the tableau inputs, not inversion-vector targets. Each pairwise bit is balanced by a swap involution.
independent_verification.decisive_check: Derive q=(1/2-ap)/(1-a) and substitute into q(1-p)^2+(1-q)p^2: 1/4+((1+a)/(1-a))(p-1/2)^2. Fresh exact rational checks for three fractions and three admissible means confirm the identity. Coordinate averaging cannot lower the .25 bound; .21 is not a rounding edge.
independent_verification.counterevidence: Different historical encoding, weighting, incomplete data or nonstandard MSE could produce .21; a table typo could also explain it. Such possibilities limit which component is wrong, but do not make the published specifications jointly consistent. Descent bits likewise balance, and descent encoding is non-injective (132/231).
independent_verification.core_dependency: The stated representation and baseline determine the difficulty and interpretation of one main regression dataset; the contradiction is internal to the paper, independent of2026 source provenance.
independent_verification.severity_and_repair: Major retained for the RSK evaluation specification, without claiming trained-model scores false or all datasets invalid. Exact historical transformation/output and corrected table/protocol are needed.
